title: hyper 6: the client kernel and renderers — index.html split under the contract, goldens shared with Go
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §The client. web/index.html becomes: kernel.js (splitHash → /api/-/route → render(view, document); hashchange; the persistent <video> and reader container), renderers/*.js (library, work, artist, item, session, continue — pure functions of an envelope, a control per actions entry, never composing a URL), player.js (the device: media element, hls.js, cast, position tick, scrub, chapter ticks, end-of-passage pause, tap-to-play). Old JSON shapes and the flat /api/items read leave the client. JS tests under node --test over the Go goldens in testdata/ (copied by a go test that fails when they drift). The shell list and sw.js bump; the CI check from flickr-ake (a shell file changed without a cache bump fails the gate) lands here.

title: hyper 4: sessions are documents; a passage is session state; the 409; marks and minting server-side
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §Passages are session state. POST /api/items/{id}/play takes an optional passage {t,end,until,from,to}; answers a session envelope (GET /api/sessions/{id} too): url, method, decision trace, passage resolved (item ids, ends_at), actions progress / keep_watching / stop / next / mark_in / mark_out / link. POST progress during a passage → 409 problem+json type passage-on, remedy keep_watching; after keep_watching → 200. Direct-play sessions get a session row too (today only transcodes have ids). mark_in/mark_out post positions; actions.link and GET /api/-/passage?… answer the minted link and its sentence ('S03E22 2:22 – 14:14 of Beach Games'); the server snaps to chapters. Handler tests for the three rules. Client: setPassage/markBounds/passageLink/keepWatching read the session document; web/passage.js shrinks to the clock predicates (passageEnded, textPassageEnded); the 'End of the passage' panel renders actions.keep_watching and links.back. sw.js bump.

title: hyper 3: GET /api/library and GET /api/artists/{name}; the browser stops regrouping
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §The documents. GET /api/library: tiles in server order (shows, films, artist shelves, audio works, books), genre facets, each tile an envelope with links.self and links.artwork and a summary line; GET /api/artists/{name}: albums in year order with covers. Golden tests. Client: buildLibrary and audio.js's works()/artists() grouping deleted; renderGrid/renderShow/renderArtist read the documents; search filters the library document client-side (a filter, not a regrouping). GET /api/works/{key} (hyper 1) feeds the show and album panes. sw.js bump.

title: hyper 1: internal/hyper envelope + root, item and work documents
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §The envelope and §The documents. New package internal/hyper: Envelope, Link, Action (method, href, input sketch, label), Problem (RFC 7807 with remedy), a Doc builder; WriteDoc/WriteProblem helpers. New handlers: GET /api/ (root: profile, links to library/continue/artists/scan/system, action scan), GET /api/items/{id} (the missing route: media_info, chapters, subtitles, artwork links, links.work/prev/next, actions play/read/progress/identity/reprobe/enrich with unavailable+reason where a kind lacks one), GET /api/works/{key} (fields, members as item envelopes with chapters/sections, places as tokens WITH labels — episodes S02E05 0:00 'The Fight', chapters 1:19:00 'Chapter 03', sections ch. 7 'The Cellar' — the profile's progress, actions play/read/passage). Golden JSON tests under testdata/ per document kind (a film, a show, an audiobook, an album, a book), driven from an in-memory store. Existing routes untouched; no client change. Note for the waymark side: /-/places-style tokens now carry labels; waymark-z8u4's follow-up (a label slot in the :places recipe) can read them.

title: hyper 2: internal/passage grammar + GET /api/-/route resolves every hash
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md §Routes are resolved by the server. New package internal/passage: the grammar now in web/passage.js (splitHash-equivalent query parse, t/end/until/untilEp/ep/from/to, locators cfi:/ch:/pg:/pct:, episode codes), table-tested with the same cases as web/passage_test.mjs. New GET /api/-/route?hash=<hash>: answers {view: library|work|artist|item, document: <envelope from hyper 1>, passage: resolved or null, autoplay: bool}; resolves #/show/<title>?ep=S03E22 against the show's members, #/item/<id>, #/artist/<name>, #/, and text locators against a book's sections; an unknown title or episode is a problem+json whose remedy links the library or the show. Every hash spelling in README 'Deep links and passages' is a test row. Client: the router's parseRoute/applyRoute call the route document instead of parsing (minimal change: keep renderers as they are, feed them what the server answered); resolveShowPassage/findEpisode leave the client. sw.js bump.

title: EPIC: flickr's own hypermedia envelope — the server says what exists and what may be done; the browser renders and owns the device
description: Design: docs/hypermedia.md (decision 2026-09-07: backend-driven with flickr's own envelope, not a waymark application). Every document is {self, kind, fields…, links, actions, unavailable}; errors are RFC 7807 problem+json with a remedy; the client follows links and actions and knows only /api/ by heart. Routes resolve on the server, passages are session state with the three rules enforced there, grouping and minting leave the browser. Eight children in order; each ships green behind the existing routes until step 6 switches the client.

title: Text reads: epub books in a reader, with a locator, a fraction and passages
description: Depends on the model bead. The epub prober fills out: OPF metadata (title, creator, language, cover → data/covers/), the spine and the TOC (nav.xhtml or NCX) as Sections {order, href, title}; a reader pane in web/ on epub.js (pinned, vendored under web/vendor so the LAN-only engine loads nothing from the internet at read time) that opens the book from GET /api/items/{id}/book (the epub bytes, range-capable) and reports position as an epub CFI plus the book's own percentage — the locator rides playback_state in a new nullable locator TEXT column beside position_seconds, and the fraction law gets its text unit: progress_text 'ch. 7 · 34%' with progress 0.34; passages: #/item/<id>?from=<locator>&to=<locator> where a locator is cfi:<epubcfi>, ch:<section order> or pct:<0..1> — the reader opens at from and, on reaching to, shows 'end of the passage' and stops advancing, writing no progress while in passage mode. PDF is its own bead.
close_reason: PR #7 merged: /book route, locator column, ch. 7 · 34% text unit, vendored epub.js reader pane, text passages

title: Audio plays: audiobooks (and albums) with chapters, cover art and a fraction of the whole
description: Depends on the model bead. decision: an audio-only item direct-plays when the client takes the codec, else transcodes to aac in an audio-only HLS or a progressive stream — the pure Decide table grows audio rows; pipeline: BuildArgs for audio-only jobs (-vn, -c:a), cover art extracted once per item (attached_pic → data/covers/, served like posters); web: an audio pane (cover, title, author/artist, chapter list from media_info.chapters) reusing the HLS/direct machinery; progress: a multi-part audiobook's position is (part ordinal, seconds) and its fraction is over the sum of the parts' durations — the works feed's progress_text reads 'ch. 7 · 1:19:22 / 11:30:00' for a chaptered m4b, 'part 3 of 12 · 0:41:10' for a set; continue-listening rides the same /api/continue. Music is the same pipeline with album works and track ordinals; play-in-order only.
close_reason: PR #5 merged: audio decision table, audio-only HLS args, cover route, chaptered clock text, audio pane in web/audio.js

title: CI: tests.yml and beads-sync.yml on the self-hosted runners
description: No .github exists. Add tests.yml: on push to master, pull_request and workflow_dispatch; one job 'test' with actions/setup-go (go-version-file: go.mod, Go 1.26.x), gofmt -l check, go vet ./..., go build ./..., go test -count=1 ./... (no ffmpeg or MinIO needed: exec only lives in runtime paths); runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }} so it moves to the fleet the moment the owner registers runners for this repo — the current fleet is REPO-scoped to ckopsa/waymark (REPO_URL in github-runner.hcl), so flickr needs its own registration; say so in a header comment. concurrency cancel-in-progress per ref; actions/cache for GOMODCACHE and GOCACHE keyed on go.sum. Add beads-sync.yml mirrored from waymark's (branch master, bd v1.2.2 cached build, bootstrap → import → dolt push) so an agent's committed .beads/issues.jsonl reaches refs/dolt/data. Fill CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section with the real commands and the CI-is-the-gate rule.
close_reason: PR #1 merged: tests.yml (gofmt/vet/build/test, CI_RUNNER var → ubuntu-latest fallback), beads-sync.yml, CLAUDE.md, first beads export

title: Passage sessions in the player: start there, stop there, and never move the person's saved place
description: The deep-link grammar, stable and documented in README: #/item/<id>?t=<start_seconds>&end=<end_seconds> for audio/video; &until=<item_id> bounds an episode run (auto-advance stops after that item); text passages are ?from=<locator>&to=<locator> (the reader bead honours them; this bead parses and passes them through). Player behaviour: (1) t wins over saved progress — playItem(item, startAt) already takes a start; (2) at end the player pauses, fires no up-next and shows 'end of the passage' with a 'keep watching' button that leaves passage mode; (3) the scrubber marks both ends; (4) a passage session writes NO progress — neither POST /api/progress on pause/end nor the natural-end write — because a scene replayed for a talk is not where the person is in the film (guard every write site with a passageActive flag; test the guard in main_test where progress is posted); (5) cast: castLoad carries t and the receiver is told the end (or the sender polls and stops it). One item first; episode runs via until. Keep the URL the single source of truth: parseRoute reads the query part of the hash.
close_reason: PR #2 merged: passage grammar (item + show forms), start/stop/no-progress rules, web/passage.js + 19 node tests, README section

title: The model learns medium: video, audio and text, from the scanner to the works feed
description: Foundation for the audio and text beads; nothing plays yet. model: MediaInfo.Medium ("video" | "audio" | "text"), Identity.Kind vocabulary grows audiobook_part, track, book beside movie/episode/extra/unknown; scanner: an admitted-extension table per medium (.m4b .m4a .mp3 .flac .opus .ogg → audio; .epub → text; .pdf recorded as a later bead), Identify learns the directory grammars Audiobooks/<Author>/<Title>/<part>, Music/<Artist>/<Album>/<NN Title>, Books/<Author>/<Title>.epub (author and title from directories, part/track ordinal from a leading number, a year in parentheses anywhere), and routes probing by medium — ffprobe for audio (chapters, duration, codec, embedded cover as attached_pic), a text prober stub that reads the epub container.xml → OPF for title/creator/spine (the reader bead fills it out); works.Build groups parts into an audiobook work, tracks into an album work, a book into itself; /api/works and /api/feed/media carry kind and medium; README documents the grammar. Table-tested like Identify is today. Waymark's mirror reads kind and medium from the feed (its own bead).
close_reason: PR #3 merged: Medium on MediaInfo, audiobook/album/book grammars, epub probe, works with medium/author/part_count, 415 for non-video play

title: EPIC: flickr serves everything the house owns — video, audio and text — and addresses a passage of any of it
description: Owner 2026-09-07. Today flickr serves movies and shows. The house also owns audiobooks, music and ebooks, and the day plan wants to launch not a work but a PASSAGE of one: a scene from 1:19:00 to 1:24:30, chapter 7 of an audiobook, pages 213–240, episodes 5–6. Two halves. (1) MEDIUM: the model, the scanner and the works API learn audio and text beside video — Audiobooks/, Music/ and Books/ directory grammars, an audio-only probe and pipeline, an epub prober and a reader — so every kind is a work with a position in its own unit and a fraction beside it (waymark's fraction law). (2) PASSAGE: a stable deep-link grammar (#/item/<id>?t=<s>&end=<s> for audio/video, ?from=<locator>&to=<locator> for text, &until=<item> for an episode run) that the player honours — start there over saved progress, stop at the end mark, no up-next, and NEVER write the passage's position over the person's saved place — plus a way to make one while watching (mark in, mark out, copy the link). Waymark's side (a passage launch on decisions, mirroring the new kinds) is its own epic there, cross-referenced. CI on the runners comes first so every bead below lands green.
close_reason: All eight children merged (PRs #1–#8): CI on the cluster, medium model, passages, mark in/out, audio, EPUB, music, PDF

title: Hash routing + server-derived continue-watching in UI
description: #/show/<key>, #/item/<id> routes (back button, shareable deep links for waymark :origin affordances); continue-watching row switches from localStorage heuristics to GET /api/continue.

title: Waymark-facing self-description: works projection, per-audience progress, cursored feed
description: Server-side works view (one entity per show/movie with work_key), per-(work,audience) derived progress/status, monotonic-sequence change cursor, GET /api/works + /api/continue + /api/feed/media. Authority stays mirror-ignorant; all endpoints are generic self-description.

title: PWA + browse polish (genre facets, richer episode lists)
description: manifest.json + service worker for phone installability; UI genre filter chips from enrichment.genres; episode rows show episode titles/stills when enriched; continue-watching row on home.

title: Per-episode + genre TMDB enrichment
description: Episode-level metadata (title/overview/still thumbnail per episode via TMDB season endpoints) and genres on show/movie enrichment — enables episode lists that look like Jellyfin's and genre browse. Key-optional like existing enrichment.

title: External subtitle sidecars (.srt/.ass next to videos in bucket)
description: Sidecar subtitle objects adjacent to video keys are currently invisible. Scan discovers them, lists them in media_info.subtitles with external:true, serves via the existing .vtt endpoint (ordinals continue after embedded tracks). Language from filename suffix (.en.srt).

title: Audio track selection
description: Probe currently records only the FIRST audio stream; multi-language files lose their other tracks. Probe all audio streams (like subtitles: ordinal/codec/language), let the capability/play request pick one, map it in the pipeline.

title: Bitmap subtitle support via burn-in
description: PGS/VobSub tracks are probed and listed but marked unsupported (no OCR). For clients selecting a bitmap track, offer burn-in: decision engine gains a subtitle dimension (burn-in forces video re-encode), pipeline adds overlay filter before the ABR split.

title: hyper 8: README's API and deep-links sections rewritten around the envelope
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md. The API table becomes the documents table; 'Deep links and passages' says the server resolves them and the three rules are the server's; a 'Reading a document' section shows one envelope and how a client walks links and actions; the design-notes list gets note 17 citing docs/hypermedia.md. After hyper 6.

title: hyper 5: the reader reads documents — read action, text passages and locator progress through the session
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md. An item envelope's actions.read (a book) opens the reader with the document (links.book, sections, the profile's locator); text passages come resolved from /api/-/route (from/to as section indexes or CFIs) and ride a session like a timed one, so a locator progress write during a text passage is the same 409; keep_reading is keep_watching. reader.js/pdfreader.js take a document instead of an item + guessed URLs. Tests: the text rows of the route resolver; a locator write during a passage refused.

title: CI: a shell file changed without a sw.js cache bump fails the gate
description: web/sw.js is cache-first for the SHELL list and the browser only re-checks sw.js itself, so a change to index.html, passage.js, audio.js, reader.js or pdfreader.js without a CACHE version bump never reaches a browser that has the old shell (bit twice on 2026-09-07: PR #11 and the tap-to-play fix). Add a step to tests.yml: if the diff against the base touches any SHELL path and web/sw.js's CACHE constant is unchanged, fail with a sentence naming the rule. Better still, derive the cache name from a content hash of the shell at build time so the bump is automatic.

title: Make a passage while watching: mark in, mark out, copy the link
description: The producer side of passages. While playing, two chips — 'mark in' and 'mark out' — set the passage bounds at the current position (chapter starts offered as snap points from media_info.chapters, which the scrubber already ticks); a third, 'copy passage link', puts #/item/<id>?t=&end= on the clipboard and shows it as text for a phone with no clipboard API. For an episode run, marking out on a later episode sets &until. No storage: a passage is a URL, and the house's decision rows are where it is kept.
close_reason: PR #4 merged: Mark in/out chips with chapter snap, copy passage link panel, until= for episode runs, 31 passage tests

title: Sweep data/streams on startup (orphaned session dirs survive restarts)
description: Session state is in-memory; an alloc restart kills ffmpeg but leaves the session's HLS dir on the persistent volume forever (observed: one stale dir post-deploy). Fix: on startup, remove all entries under data/streams — no session can survive a restart by construction. One rm in main() before NewSessionManager.

title: Verify subtitles + ABR on the real TV
description: Deferred 2026-07-27 ~1am because the Office TV was powered off (and the Hub Max refuses cast connections from the dev box — see home-infrastructure flickr-stream KNOWN-ISSUES #7). Run: FLICKR_SERVER=https://stream.kopsa.info .venv/bin/python scripts/cast_harness.py --device 'Office TV' and a manual cast with a subtitle track selected.

title: rkmpp hardware DECODE
description: Only encode is VPU-offloaded; decode and filters run on CPU — the bottleneck for hevc sources and trickplay generation on the orangepi. jellyfin-ffmpeg ships rkmpp decoders; wire -hwaccel rkmpp into the pipeline (careful: filter chain then needs hwdownload or rga-based scale).

title: hyper 7: the Cast receiver reads the session document
description: Per docs/hypermedia.md. The receiver (or the sender's cast bridge) is handed the session envelope: url, passage ends_at, next; the sender stops composing what the receiver plays from raw fields. Optional; after hyper 4.

title: PDF reads: page ranges through pdf.js
description: After the epub reader. .pdf under Books/ becomes a book item with medium text; a pdf.js reader pane; locator pg:<n>; passages ?from=pg:213&to=pg:240; progress_text 'p. 213 / 400'.
close_reason: PR #8 merged: ProbePDF page count, pg: locator, p. 213 / 400, vendored pdf.js reader pane

title: Music: albums as works, tracks in order, an artist page
description: After the audio bead plays a single item. Music/<Artist>/<Album>/ works with track ordinals, play-in-order across tracks with the audio pane, an artist tile grouping albums; no playlists, no shuffle, no lyrics — the house's use is a record on in the kitchen.
close_reason: PR #6 merged: TrackTitle, /api/artists, artist tiles and #/artist/<name> view, tracks by title in the pane

title: Triage probe failures
description: A handful of objects fail probing every scan: csi-fs/Movies/Dune (2021)/Dune_t00.mkv (MakeMKV artifact, possibly truncated) and a few others surfaced in scan status errors. Inspect with ffprobe directly; fix or delete the objects, or mark them ignorable.

title: Register custom Cast receiver + use telemetry
description: web/receiver.html (CAF receiver with telemetry to /api/telemetry, ?debug=1 overlay) is deployed at https://stream.kopsa.info/receiver.html. Needs: $5 Google Cast console registration, register device serials, app id into sender localStorage.castAppId. Then receiver-side stats close the observability loop and chrome://inspect works against the TV.
